title: Why Service Is A Powerful Classroom Management Strategy gement-strategy/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin presents encouraging student service-orientation as a powerful classroom management strategy, arguing that it builds empathy, reduces bullying, improves self-worth, and helps students see how their disruptive behavior affects those around them. He offers three concrete starting steps: explicitly defining service to students as an active form of helpfulness that isn't waited on but sought out; modeling it constantly through the teacher's own small gestures like greeting students and picking up dropped items; and physically going out to serve the wider school community, such as cleaning shared spaces or helping in another classroom. He notes today's students tend to embrace service readily, and that good classroom management creates the surplus time needed to fit it in, with most administrators supportive when given advance notice. The piece frames service as both a calming, character-building practice and a direct behavior-improvement tool.
points: Encouraging student service is presented as a powerful classroom management strategy that builds empathy and reduces bullying.
Three starting steps are given: explicitly define service for students, model it constantly through small teacher gestures, and physically go serve the wider school community.
Service is defined specifically as an active form of helpfulness—something sought out, not waited for when asked.
Today's students are described as unusually quick to embrace service compared to prior generations.
Good classroom management is said to create the surplus time needed to incorporate service, with administrators typically supportive when informed in advance.
quotes: Encouraging your students to become service-oriented is a powerful classroom management strategy.
It causes them to see their classmates as people just like them, with the same hopes, feelings, and struggles.
Service is an active form of helpfulness. Meaning, you don’t wait until someone asks. It’s something you look for and act upon, even when it’s inconvenient.
Your students are more influenced by what you do than what you say.
As for finding the time for it, with good classroom management comes the freedom not to have to rush through anything . It buys you oceans of time few other teachers enjoy.
Make your classroom more than just the acquisition of knowledge. Develop the whole person by being a classroom defined by service.
